source_user: A long-context workload intermittently hits OOM after several concurrent requests. Give a prioritized diagnosis and mitigations. Scenario variant 73: include an explicit falsifiable hypothesis and a controlled experiment.
source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. Minimum technical points: measure per-request KV growth and allocator fragmentation; check max sequence and batch; inspect active sequences; test paged/prefix cache, admission control, quantization, and context limits.
corrected_answer:
Assumptions and containment: the failing allocator is not known; distinguish GPU device OOM from host, pinned-memory, or swap exhaustion before changing configuration. Record model/runtime revision, precision, parallelism, GPU capacity in GiB, allocator settings, scheduler limits, max sequence and batch/token budgets, active-sequence counts, and prompt/output-length distributions. Use a staging replay first; temporarily cap concurrency and reject or queue requests that exceed a conservative token budget rather than risking repeated production OOMs.

Prioritized falsifiable hypothesis (variant 73): H1 is that concurrent live KV-cache bytes plus allocator fragmentation consume the usable device headroom. Measure per-request KV growth in bytes and tokens, active sequences, allocated versus reserved bytes, largest free block, and free headroom at each admission and failure. H1 is supported only if matched prompt/output-length strata show higher OOM probability with live KV bytes/active sequences and a smaller free margin or larger reserved-minus-allocated gap. Falsify H1 if KV remains bounded and fragmentation is low while a prefill workspace, activation, communication buffer, host allocation, duplicated prefix entry, retained post-completion block, or runtime leak spikes; also check max-sequence/batch overshoot.

Controlled experiment: capture a fixed representative trace, stratified by prompt length, output cap, and concurrency, and randomize paired runs of baseline versus one change at a time (paged KV/prefix sharing, admission control, lower max context, quantized KV, or lower precision only if numerically validated). Warm up identically, repeat enough times to observe failures, and keep model, inputs, clocks, and hardware fixed. Log request admission/start/end/rejection/OOM, per-request KV allocation and release, cache hits/evictions, allocator snapshots, GPU/host/pinned/swap usage, prefill/decode workspaces, and correctness plus TTFT/TPOT/throughput/queue latency. Report OOMs and rejected requests over all attempted requests, with confidence intervals; do not call an intervention effective from a single successful run.

Mitigations in priority order: enforce token-aware admission with headroom and bounded queueing; cap context/output and batch limits with explicit user-visible rejection; use paged KV and prefix sharing only after verifying reference lifetime, isolation, and correctness; tune allocator/defragmentation or restart workers only as containment; evaluate KV quantization/offload with measured latency, bandwidth, and numerical-quality gates. Roll back any change if OOM, correctness failures, tail latency, queueing, or error/rejection rates exceed predeclared baseline bounds; canary gradually and retain a kill switch. Evidence required: allocator/runtime documentation and synchronized traces plus repeated matched baseline/treatment results on the target hardware.
risks: The exact KV layout, allocator counters, paging behavior, and OOM source are backend-specific; estimates must not be presented as measured facts.
Quantization, offload, prefix sharing, and allocator changes can affect correctness, isolation, bandwidth, and tail latency.
evidence_required: Confirm device/host OOM attribution and units from synchronized runtime and hardware telemetry.
Run repeated randomized matched replay on the target model, engine, and hardware with predefined OOM, correctness, latency, and rejection gates.

Falsify H1 if KV remains bounded and fragmentation is low while a prefill workspace, activation, communication buffer, host allocation, duplicated prefix entry, retained post-completion block, or runtime leak spikes; also check max-sequence/batch overshoot.

Controlled experiment: capture a fixed representative trace, stratified by prompt length, output cap, and concurrency, and randomize paired runs of baseline versus one change at a time (paged KV/prefix sharing, admission control, lower max context, quantized KV, or lower precision only if numerically validated). Warm up identically, repeat enough times to observe failures, and keep model, inputs, clocks, and hardware fixed. Log request admission/start/end/rejection/OOM, per-request KV allocation and release, cache hits/evictions, allocator snapshots, GPU/host/pinned/swap usage, prefill/decode workspaces, and correctness plus TTFT/TPOT/throughput/queue latency. Report OOMs and rejected requests over all attempted requests, with confidence intervals; do not call an intervention effective from a single successful run.

Mitigations in priority order: enforce token-aware admission with headroom and bounded queueing; cap context/output and batch limits with explicit user-visible rejection; use paged KV and prefix sharing only after verifying reference lifetime, isolation, and correctness; tune allocator/defragmentation or restart workers only as containment; evaluate KV quantization/offload with measured latency, bandwidth, and numerical-quality gates. Roll back any change if OOM, correctness failures, tail latency, queueing, or error/rejection rates exceed predeclared baseline bounds; canary gradually and retain a kill switch. Evidence required: allocator/runtime documentation and synchronized traces plus repeated matched baseline/treatment results on the target hardware.
risks: The exact KV layout, allocator counters, paging behavior, and OOM source are backend-specific; estimates must not be presented as measured facts.
Quantization, offload, prefix sharing, and allocator changes can affect correctness, isolation, bandwidth, and tail latency.
evidence_required: Confirm device/host OOM attribution and units from synchronized runtime and hardware telemetry.
Run repeated randomized matched replay on the target model, engine, and hardware with predefined OOM, correctness, latency, and rejection gates.
